questions.question: Give an example of healthcare demand being income elastic.
questions.solution_html:
• Income elastic demand means demand changes with the changes in income-Example —
  • preference for private hospital care in Kerala- When income rises, people prefer private
  • hospitals instead of public ones-Health services are seen as a superior good-Shows positive
  • relation between income and healthcare demand
questions.final_answer: relation between income and healthcare demand
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the poverty–malnutrition trap.
questions.solution_html:
• Poverty–malnutrition trap means a cycle linking low income and poor health -Poor people
  • cannot afford enough nutritious food - Leads to low productivity and poor health-Low
  • productivity reduces income again-The cycle of poverty and malnutrition continues across
  • generations.
questions.final_answer: generations
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What are the key objectives of the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)?
questions.solution_html:
• NRHM started in 2005 to improve rural health care-Aim — provide accessible, affordable
  • and quality health services-Reduce maternal and infant mortality-Strengthen public health
  • infrastructure-Promote community participation through ASHA workers-Focus on primary
  • health care and rural poor.
questions.final_answer: health care and rural poor
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the impact of institutional discrimination on the healthcare access and health outcomes of marginalized communities.
questions.solution_html:
• Institutional discrimination limits equal access to healthcare-Marginalized groups face
  • neglect and bias in hospitals- Leads to poor health outcomes and higher disease rates-Weak
  • implementation of inclusive health policies -Reduces trust in public health systems-Deepens
  • social and economic inequality.
questions.final_answer: social and economic inequality
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Suggest a plan to make public hospitals better by reducing waiting time and giving more personal care to patients
questions.solution_html:
• Introduce online appointment and queue system - Increase number of doctors and nurses
  • Use patient feedback for service improvement-Apply time-based performance monitoring
  • Create separate counters for emergency and routine cases-Promote staff training for personal
  • care and empathy
questions.final_answer: care and empathy

questions.question: Write any two mortality indicators measured in NFHS. / Assess the significance of the National Health Mission (NHM) in strengthening
questions.solution_html:
• Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) – number of deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live
  • births- Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) – number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
  • Both are key mortality indicators used in National Family Health Survey (NFHS)
questions.final_answer: Both are key mortality indicators used in National Family Health Survey (NFHS)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: / India's public health infrastructure.

questions.question: Discuss the role of health as a component of human capital. Give an example.
questions.solution_html:
• Health is key part of human capital-Healthy people are more productive and efficient
  • Good health improves learning and skill development-Reduces absenteeism and medical costs
  • -Example – healthier workers in Kerala earn more and contribute to economy.
questions.final_answer: -Example – healthier workers in Kerala earn more and contribute to economy

questions.question: How research play a vital role in fostering competiveness?
questions.solution_html:
• Research helps identify new methods and technologies - Improves skills and productivity
  • of workers -Supports innovation in health and education sectors-Provides data for better
  • decision-making-Example – research in Kerala improves hospital services and teaching
  • quality.
questions.final_answer: quality

questions.question: Analyze the impact of educated migration on Kerala’s unemployment problem.
questions.solution_html:
• Educated migration reduces local job seekers in Kerala-Creates brain drain, limiting skilled
  • workforce locally-Can reduce unemployment pressure temporarily- Leads to higher
  • remittances improving household income-Impacts labor market planning and education-job
  • match in Kerala.
questions.final_answer: match in Kerala

questions.question: Mention one difference between public and private healthcare facilities in Kerala.
questions.solution_html:
• Public healthcare – government funded, low cost, serves all, focus on primary and
  • preventive care- Private healthcare – privately funded, higher cost, focus on personalized and
  • specialized care- Public facilities face overcrowding, private facilities offer shorter waiting
  • time- Both complement each other in Kerala’s health system.
questions.final_answer: time- Both complement each other in Kerala’s health system
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of a public health intervention aimed at reducing morbidity.
questions.solution_html:
• Assess change in disease incidence before and after intervention- Example – immunization
  • programs reducing child morbidity in Kerala -Check coverage and participation of target
  • population-Evaluate improvement in health outcomes and reduced hospital visits-Identify
  • challenges and gaps for further policy action.
questions.final_answer: challenges and gaps for further policy action
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the role of social reformers in Kerala’s educational progress.
questions.solution_html:
• Social reformers-Examples – Sree Narayana Guru, Ayyankali, and Chattampi Swamikal
  • Social reformers spread awareness about literacy and equality- Reduced social barriers to
  • education- Promoted education for all, including women and lower castes- Reduced social
  • barriers to education-Founded schools and colleges in Kerala.
  • Part-C
questions.final_answer: Part-C
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does investment in public health promote inclusive and sustainable development?
questions.solution_html:
• Investment in public health improves population health and life expectancy-Healthy people
  • are more productive and contribute to the economy - Reduces medical expenses for poor
  • households, promoting financial inclusion-Strengthens human capital, supporting skilled
  • workforce development- Promotes equity by providing access to healthcare for all, including
  • marginalized groups- Reduces disease burden, improving school attendance and workforce
  • participation- Example – Kerala’s NRHM and local health initiatives reduced infant mortality
  • to 7 per 1,000 (NFHS-5)-Supports sustainable development goals by improving health
  • education, and economic growth together.
questions.final_answer: education, and economic growth together
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe and distinguish the benefits of investing in education and the benefits of investing in health, as both are important parts of human capital formation?
questions.solution_html:
• Education improves knowledge, skills, and productivity of individuals-Leads to higher
  • earnings and better job opportunities-Promotes social awareness and participation in civic life
  • Health investment improves physical and mental well-being- Healthy people are more
  • productive and active in work and learning-Reduces disease burden and medical costs
  • especially for poor families-Both together strengthen human capital, enhancing economic
  • growth and development- Example – In Kerala, high literacy rate (96%) and good health
  • outcomes support skilled workforce and low infant mortality (7 per 1,000 live births, NFHS
questions.final_answer: outcomes support skilled workforce and low infant mortality (7 per 1,000 live births, NFHS
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the role of government policy measures in reducing moral hazard in the health insurance sector.
questions.solution_html:
• Moral hazard occurs when insured people overuse healthcare services-Government policies
  • reduce this risk by regulating health insurance plans- Introduces co-payments, deductibles, and
  • coverage limits to control overuse-Promotes preventive care programs to reduce long-term
  • claims- Monitors insurance companies to ensure fair pricing and claims-Encourages awareness
  • among insured individuals about responsible use of services- Example – India’s Ayushman
  • Bharat PM-JAY includes checks to prevent over-treatment-Reduces unnecessary expenses
  • improves financial sustainability, and ensures better access to essential health services
  • Supports equity and efficiency in the health sector.
questions.final_answer: Supports equity and efficiency in the health sector
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the role of local governments in public health and sanitation. How effective are they as grassroots implementers, and what limits their potential?
questions.solution_html:
• Local governments in Kerala implement primary healthcare and sanitation programs
  • Manage PHCs, Sub-Centres, waste disposal, and water supply-Promote community health
  • awareness and preventive measures-Example – Kerala Panchayats successfully implement
  • clean Kerala campaign and vector control programs- Effective as grassroots implementers due
  • to local knowledge and community participation-Limitations include fund constraints, staff
  • shortages, and coordination issues-Political interference and weak monitoring reduce
  • efficiency-Despite challenges, local governments improve access, reduce disease burden, and
  • support public health policies in rural areas- Their role is crucial for inclusive and sustainable
  • health development.
questions.final_answer: health development
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Assess how far the National Health Mission (NHM) has improved rural health services and infrastructure.
questions.solution_html:
• NHM aims to improve rural health services and infrastructure across India- Strengthened
  • Sub-Centres, PHCs, and CHCs in rural areas-Promoted maternal and child health programs
  • reducing IMR and MMR-Example – Kerala’s rural infant mortality reduced to 7 per 1,000 live
  • births (NFHS-5)-Introduced ASHA workers for community health outreach- Improved
  • availability of medicines, diagnostic facilities, and trained staff-Challenges remain in remote
  • areas, staff shortages, and facility maintenance- Overall, NHM significantly enhanced access
  • quality, and equity of rural health services-Supports inclusive health development and reduces
  • regional health disparities.
questions.final_answer: regional health disparities
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What are the key factors and main areas of government spending on education? / Give examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Government spending on education focuses on access, quality, and equity-Key factors
  • include literacy goals, human capital formation, and inclusive growth- Main areas of spending
  • – school infrastructure, teacher salaries, training, and scholarships-Investment in Mid-Day
  • Meal Scheme improves student attendance and nutrition- Funding for higher education
  • research, and vocational training promotes skill development-Example – Kerala spends about
  • 6% of its state budget on education- Central schemes like Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan and NEP
  • 2020 reforms support education quality. Aim – build an educated, skilled, and employable
  • population for sustainable development.
questions.final_answer: population for sustainable development
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does the teacher-student ratio impact learning outcomes?
questions.solution_html:
• Teacher-student ratio means number of students per teacher-A low ratio allows more
  • attention to each student-Improves classroom interaction, learning quality, and academic
  • performance-A high ratio leads to overcrowding and less personal attention- Impacts student
  • motivation, participation, and understanding- Better ratio helps achieve equity and quality
  • education, key goal of NEP 2020-Thus, it directly influences learning outcomes and human
  • capital formation.
questions.final_answer: capital formation
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically evaluate whether NEP 2020 addresses the problem of inequality in education.
questions.solution_html:
• NEP 2020 aims to provide inclusive and equitable education for all- Focus on Early
  • Childhood Care, universal access, and foundational literacy. Promotes flexible curriculum and
  • multilingual education to reduce social barriers- Targets dropout reduction through open
  • schooling and multiple entry–exit options- Encourages digital learning, but digital divide limits
  • rural participation- Supports gender inclusion through Gender Inclusion Fund- Yet, funding
  • gaps and implementation inequality between states remain- Kerala already performs well, but
  • poorer states lag behind-NEP 2020 is a progressive step, but needs strong public investment
  • for true equality- Hence, policy is promising but not fully effective in reducing inequality.
questions.final_answer: for true equality- Hence, policy is promising but not fully effective in reducing inequality
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically evaluate the Kerala Model of development.
questions.solution_html:
• Kerala Model shows high human development with low per capita income-Strong focus
  • on education, health, and social welfare-Achieved literacy rate of 96.2% (Census 2021) —
  • highest in India-Life expectancy about 75 years, similar to developed countries- Success due
  • to public investment and social reforms by leaders and movements-Promoted gender equality
  • public health, and land reforms- Criticism: High unemployment, migration dependency, and
  • fiscal stress-Economic growth slower than social development-Environmental and ageing
  • population issues rising- Overall, Kerala Model is socially progressive but economically
  • imbalanced.
questions.final_answer: imbalanced
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the importance of healthcare financing in Kerala’s health sector.
questions.solution_html:
• Healthcare financing means mobilising and using funds for health services-In Kerala, it
  • helps to establish and maintain quality public health infrastructure-Supports primary health
  • centres, hospitals and Medical Colleges, medical research and preventive care-Ensures
  • equitable access to health services for all citizens-State government funds, NHM, and insurance
  • schemes like Karunya Arogya Suraksha Padhathi are major sources-Helps to reduce out-of
  • pocket expenditure- Enables universal health coverage and disease control programs-Important
  • for sustainability of Kerala’s high health indicators-Encourages public-private partnerships for
  • better service delivery.
questions.final_answer: better service delivery
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
